Primary sources establish both Toronto settlement/residence and a longstanding Bahamas community connection. Principal residence is corrected to Canada on terminal evidence; no unsupported dual citizenship or exact residency allocation is proposed.

Forbes was searched first and verified under Loretta Robinson. LinkedIn, Instagram, personal website, Facebook, Twitter/X, YouTube and TikTok searches yielded institutional coverage or unrelated namesakes, including the Florida romance writer Loretta C. Rogers. No attributable personal account was found. Vimeo, Flickr, Trip Advisor and Zillow searches also produced no supported account. Institutional videos are not personal channels. The verified company biography is labelled Company Website.

No direct beneficial-ownership document for the input vessels is asserted. The exact-name, age, nationality, personal article and Bahamas connections establish the target. Personal illness and family disputes are excluded. The obituary hosting service and direct company PDF request were inaccessible; the SEC complete relevant text and other primary bodies were read. A book-preview search lead about advanced family capital was not recoverable in the opened preview, so its specific amount and mechanism are not treated as verified evidence.

The canonical verified personal page is https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Rogers . The source already has a Wikipedia type with a malformed spaced URL. biography.plain_text: Loretta Rogers was a London-born Canadian businesswoman and philanthropist who helped finance her husband Ted Rogers's early communications business. A longstanding company director, she later shared in the inheritance of his Rogers Communications stake. She settled in Toronto after their marriage and became a major supporter of medical research and education.

long_biography.plain_text:
Canadian businesswoman Loretta Rogers studied fine arts at the University of Miami and contributed paintings to children's books. Her illustrations appeared alongside work by wildlife artist Robert Bateman in books including Larry the Loon, which recounts efforts to care for an injured bird. She also taught painting to friends through the Tobin Island School of Fine Arts.

At Toronto Western Hospital, Rogers launched a campaign to renovate the critical care facilities, seeking better surroundings for patients, families and staff. Her husband pledged the funds to name the new centre in her honour. She later made a personal gift establishing a heart function research chair held by cardiologist Heather Ross.
